equation_request.abstract: We analyze the performance of a generalized Kitaev’s phase estimation algorithm where $N$ phase gates, acting on $M$ qubits prepared in a product state, may be distributed in an arbitrary way. Unlike the standard algorithm, where the mean square error scales as $1/N$, the optimal generalizations offer the Heisenberg $1/N^{2}$ error scaling and we show that they are in fact very close to the fundamental Bayesian estimation bound. We also demonstrate that the optimality of the algorithm breaks down when losses are taken into account, in which case the performance is inferior to the optimal entanglement-based estimation strategies. Finally, we show that when an alternative resource quantification is adopted, which describes the phase estimation in Shor’s algorithm more accurately, the standard Kitaev’s procedure is indeed optimal and there is no need to consider its generalized version.

specification.problem: Estimate an unknown phase phi using a generalized Kitaev scheme in which N phase gates are distributed arbitrarily among M qubits prepared in a product state, with the goal of reaching Heisenberg-type 1/N^2 mean square error scaling.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Smallest useful construction: M=2 qubits in |+> product states, with n_1 and n_2 applications of the phase gate and n_1+n_2=N, together with the mean square error definition and the scaling claims. The optimal gate distribution, the lossy analysis, the Bayesian bound derivation and the Shor-type resource quantification are outside this scope.

equations.label: Resource constraint
equations.description: N phase gates are distributed in an arbitrary way among the M qubits.
equations.abstract_quote: where $N$ phase gates, acting on $M$ qubits prepared in a product state, may be distributed in an arbitrary way
equations.justification: The abstract states that N gates act on M qubits with an arbitrary distribution. The sum constraint is the natural formalization of this.
assumptions: Each gate acts on a single qubit
The total gate count is the resource

equations.label: Single-qubit state after n_k gates
equations.description: A qubit prepared in |+> that receives n_k phase gates U=diag(1,e^{i\varphi}).
equations.justification: Standard Kitaev-type phase encoding, assumed here for the tiny instance. The abstract does not state it.

equations.label: Product probe state
equations.description: The product state of all M qubits after the gates have been applied.
equations.abstract_quote: acting on $M$ qubits prepared in a product state
equations.justification: The abstract says the qubits are prepared in a product state. The explicit form follows from eq_2.
assumptions: The state stays a product state because there is no entangling operation

equations.label: Mean square error
equations.description: A periodic mean square error for a circular variable, which approximates the usual squared error when the error is small.
equations.justification: A common choice for phase estimation. The abstract names the mean square error but does not define it.
assumptions: The precise cost function used in the paper may differ

equations.label: Scaling claims
equations.description: Scaling of the error for the standard Kitaev algorithm and for the optimal generalized versions.
equations.abstract_quote: where the mean square error scales as $1/N$, the optimal generalizations offer the Heisenberg $1/N^{2}$ error scaling
equations.justification: These are the scalings stated in the abstract. Prefactors and the optimal distributions are not given.

registers.name: q_1..q_M
registers.size: M (taken as 2 in the tiny instance)
registers.role: probe qubits, each in a product state, each acted on by n_k phase gates

steps.description: Choose a distribution (n_1,...,n_M) with total N (for example M=2, n_1+n_2=N).
Prepare each qubit in |+> and apply n_k phase gates to qubit k.
Measure the qubits and form an estimate of phi, then evaluate its mean square error. The estimator is not specified in the abstract.
Compare the error scaling against the 1/N and 1/N^2 claims.

specification.measurement: Not specified in the abstract. A Kitaev-type single-qubit measurement in the X/Y basis of each qubit is a plausible assumption.
specification.classical_postprocessing: Not specified in the abstract. The estimate would be combined from the single-qubit outcomes, for example by a Bayesian or maximum-likelihood estimator.
assumptions: The scope is M=2 qubits with |+> inputs and the ideal lossless setting.
The phase gate is diag(1,e^{i phi}).
The mean square error is the periodic cost in eq_4.
missing_information: The optimal gate distributions n_k and the proofs of the 1/N^2 scaling
The Bayesian bound and its comparison
The loss model and the comparison with entanglement-based strategies
